messages:
sam: hey team, new hire here. trying to build runtime on Ubuntu 22.04 VM (host has an NVIDIA A40). following BUILD.md but unit tests fail when trying to load CUDA symbols at runtime. stacktrace shows: `dlopen(...libcuda.so...) failed: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory`. any quick checks?

sam: `nvidia-smi` prints Driver Version: 535.86.10. CUDA toolkit installed from apt is 11.8 in /usr/local/cuda-11.8.

noah: welcome! :wave: that error usually means the runtime can't find libcuda on ld path. On Ubuntu with driver installed from NVIDIA apt repo the libcuda is typically under `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1` or in `/usr/lib/nvidia-535/libcuda.so`. run `ldconfig -p | grep libcuda` to see registered locations.

sam: `ldconfig -p | grep libcuda` returns nothing. weird. I installed the driver via the .run file a while back.

alexa: .run installer sometimes doesn't run ldconfig or place symlinks. Check `/usr/lib/nvidia-*/libcuda.so*`. If present, create a symlink in `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/` and run `sudo ldconfig`. Example: `sudo ln -s /usr/lib/nvidia-535/libcuda.so.1 /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so` then `sudo ldconfig`.

sam: found `/usr/lib/nvidia-535/libcuda.so.1`. created symlink and ldconfig. `ldconfig -p | grep libcuda` now shows an entry.

sam: rebuild and rerun tests, new error: `undefined symbol: cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain` when loading plugin. Looks like a symbol mismatch.

noah: that symbol suggests the driver in kernel/runtime doesn't match the CUDA userland headers. `cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain` was introduced in CUDA 11.x but if your driver is older it might not expose it. What does `nvidia-smi` show for CUDA Compatibility?

sam: nvidia-smi shows `CUDA Version: 12.0` but toolkit is 11.8. Could be leftover libs from previous installs.

alexa: safest path: reinstall driver via the distro package (apt) so libs end up in standard paths and DKMS manages kernel modules. If you prefer runfile, use `--silent --disable-nouveau --dkms` flags and re-run the installer to rebuild kernel module against current kernel headers. Also remove old `/usr/local/cuda` symlink and re-create to point to the toolkit you want.

sam: I'm on a corporate VM, kernel headers were missing earlier which messed up DKMS. Installed `linux-headers-$(uname -r)` and re-ran the driver installer with `--dkms`. driver install completed and `nvidia-smi` shows same version. But runtime still errors.

noah: check `strings /usr/lib/nvidia-535/libcuda.so.1 | grep cuDevicePrimaryCtxRetain` to see if symbol present.

sam: symbol present. but the shared object the test loads seems to reference a different SONAME. `readelf -d bin/test_plugin | grep NEEDED` shows `libcuda.so.1` so it should link.

alexa: could be that your build linked against static CUDA (libcudart_static.a) accidentally, causing mixed ABI issues. Did you build with BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON and CMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON?

sam: I used the default build script which sets BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF. Hmm.

noah: Try clean build with `-DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON -DCMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE=ON -DENABLE_CUDA=ON`. Also check that `cmake` picks up the correct CUDA toolkit with `-- Found CUDA: /usr/local/cuda-11.8 (found version "11.8")` output.

sam: rebuilt with those flags. linking succeeded locally, but when running tests inside the runtime dev container, plugin dlopen fails with same symbol error. Host works, container doesn't.

alexa: container runtime needs nvidia-container-toolkit to expose GPUs and drivers into the container. Do you run docker with `--gpus all`? If the container image lacks `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1` or can't see host drivers, dlopen will fail.

sam: running `docker run --gpus all -it runtime-dev:local /bin/bash` then inside `ldconfig -p | grep libcuda` shows nothing. I guess the toolkit isn't mounted.

infra-bot: [infra-bot] Note: Docker host does not have nvidia-container-toolkit configured for legacy runtime. See infra status page.

noah: Oof. On our infra we rely on `nvidia-container-toolkit` + proper daemon.json config to mount `/usr/lib/nvidia-<version>` into the container. Ask infra team to flip it, or test locally with `--volume /usr/lib/nvidia-535:/usr/lib/nvidia-535:ro` and `--volume /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1:ro` as workaround.

sam: I mounted the host libs into container and relaunch. inside container `ldconfig -p | grep libcuda` now shows libcuda and tests pass. thanks!

alexa: for a long term fix we should document that dev containers require `nvidia-container-toolkit` on hosts or have the image include a stub `libcuda` that forwards calls (not recommended). Please open a short PR to dev docs.

sam: will do. last q: any tips to avoid changing host drivers while onboarding?

noah: use a disposable VM or cloud instance for driver experiments, or use our CI's reproducible dev container (ask @eng-runtime-oncall for image + build task). we also have `dev/containers/runtime-dev.Dockerfile` which works if host has the toolkit configured.

eng-runtime-oncall: ping me and I'll share the verified image tag and CI job to run locally. Also we can spin up a GPU playground VM for you for a bit.

sam: thanks everyone, big help. I'll open the doc PR and ping infra about the toolkit so new hires don't hit this. :raised_hands:
